chains.title: HOXB13 binds the T allele at the rs339331 enhancer and modulates RFX6 in prostate cells
chains.cell_type: prostate cancer (LNCaP clone FGC and PCa tumors)

links.claim: HOXB13 has its own QBiC-SELEX model, and the ref T allele binds more strongly (effect -4.771, z -103.49; ref site 99.9th vs alt 97.2nd percentile). E09d places a HOXB13-containing GATA2/SMAD4 complex at the rs339331 enhancer, but base-level allele-specific HOXB13 occupancy is not directly shown.
rs339331 lies in dELS EH38E2496909, and E09d reports a HOXB13/GATA2/SMAD4 complex at this 6q22 enhancer.
The HOXB13-containing complex at this enhancer is reported to increase RFX6 expression; RFX6 is also the nearest protein-coding gene and the top L2G gene at the locus.
The proposed mechanism is in prostate cancer cells/tumors, where HOXB13 is a lineage factor; the case expression context is LNCaP clone FGC.

rs339331 is strongly associated with prostate cancer and the rs339331-RFX6/6q22 locus is implicated in PCa risk/progression, but the allelic direction is unresolved: E06 reports C as the effect allele, while this chain's QBiC prediction is that T binds HOXB13 more.

predictions: Allele-specific HOXB13 ChIP or footprinting in prostate cancer cells shows more HOXB13 on the T allele than the C allele at rs339331.
RFX6 expression or enhancer activity is higher with the T allele and is reduced by HOXB13 loss in this context.
A T-vs-C reporter assay at the rs339331 enhancer shows allele-specific activity that depends on the HOXB13 site.
falsified_if: HOXB13 does not occupy rs339331 in prostate cancer cells.
The C allele, not T, shows higher HOXB13 occupancy at this base.
HOXB13 loss does not change RFX6 expression or enhancer activity at this element.

RFX6 expression is not allele-specific at rs339331 after controlling for linked variants.

chains.title: AR binds the T allele at rs339331 and increases RFX6 in prostate cancer

links.claim: Literature reports rs339331 in a reprogrammed AR binding site and the T allele enhancing AR occupancy (E09c), but AR has no QBiC-SELEX model in the provided evidence, and E04/E18 find no LNCaP AR ChIP peak over the variant. AR occupancy in LNCaP is therefore not established.
rs339331 lies in dELS EH38E2496909, and E09c places rs339331 in a reprogrammed AR binding site in prostate cancer tumors.
RFX6 is the nearest protein-coding gene and the top L2G gene at the locus, and E09b names the rs339331-RFX6/6q22 locus.
The AR mechanism is proposed in prostate cancer tumors, not specifically in LNCaP clone FGC; E04 reports 0 LNCaP ChIP peaks over the variant.
The prostate cancer association is strong, but the direction is unresolved: E06 reports C as the effect allele, while E09c calls T the risk allele and says T increases AR occupancy.

predictions: Allele-specific AR ChIP in prostate cancer cells shows more AR on the T allele than the C allele at rs339331.
RFX6 expression or enhancer activity is AR-dependent and tracks the T allele in AR-positive prostate cancer cells.
AR perturbation reduces RFX6 expression or the relevant prostate cancer phenotype.
falsified_if: AR does not occupy this base in prostate cancer cells.
The C allele, not T, shows higher AR occupancy.
RFX6 expression is not affected by AR or by this allele in prostate cancer cells.

chains.title: PKNOX1 binds the C allele weakly at rs339331 outside prostate context

links.claim: PKNOX1 QBiC-SELEX predicts the alt C allele binds more strongly (z 11.43, effect +0.521, above the gate), but the best site is weak on both alleles (ref 86.1st, alt 96.7th percentile). PKNOX1 ChIP contains the variant only in HEK293T, not LNCaP, so prostate-cell occupancy is not established.
The variant lies in dELS EH38E2496909, and PKNOX1 ChIP-seq peaks containing the variant exist in other biosamples.
RFX6 is the nearest gene and the best-supported L2G target, but there is no direct PKNOX1-to-RFX6 evidence; this gene link is conditional.
PKNOX1 is expressed in LNCaP clone FGC (8.32 TPM), but the only ChIP peak over the variant is from HEK293T; the prostate-cell link is weak.
The locus is associated with prostate cancer, but a PKNOX1-mediated route through this weak, non-prostate-occupied site is speculative.

predictions: PKNOX1 ChIP in prostate cancer cells shows occupancy at rs339331, preferably on the C allele.
PKNOX1 perturbation changes RFX6 expression or enhancer activity in prostate cells.
The weak QBiC site is not functional unless another factor or co-factor stabilizes PKNOX1 binding.
falsified_if: PKNOX1 does not occupy this base in prostate cancer cells.
There is no allele-specific PKNOX1 binding at rs339331.
PKNOX1 loss does not affect RFX6 or enhancer activity.

Dysregulated expression or mutations of the RFX6 gene in prostate cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma, gastric cancer, melanoma, and other tumors have garnered significant interest, with studies showing that such alterations affect tumor cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, and are correlated with an unfavorable clinical prognosis in patients carrying RFX6 mutations.

Here the FinnGen cohort phenome-wide analysis, along with multiple genome-wide association studies, has consistently identified the rs339331-RFX6/6q22 locus associated with prostate cancer (PCa) risk across diverse populations.
It is uncovered that rs339331 resides in a reprogrammed androgen receptor (AR) binding site in PCa tumors, with the T risk allele enhancing AR chromatin occupancy.

Strinkingly, GATA2 and SMAD4 globally mediated inherited PCa risk and formed a transcriptional complex with HOXB13 at the PCa risk-associated rs339331/6q22 enhancer, leading to increased expression of the PCa susceptibility gene RFX6.
Notable genes of interest include HCP5, RFX6 and H3C1 for risk, and MKI67 and KLF5 for aggressive disease.

Shown: 1 of 1 occupied (0 with a strong site), 5 of 131 with unknown occupancy. Left out: 1 TFs assayed in the matching biosample and 569 assayed only elsewhere, none with a peak here; 2 bound but below 1 TPM. The gate (|z| > 4.05, Bonferroni over 997 models) marks a change QBiC-SELEX detects; it says nothing about occupancy. Effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly. In vitro binding only. Site strength is the better allele's best k-mer over the variant, as a percentile of the best model's k-mers; a strong site reaches the 97.5th. At a weak site the ChIP peak more likely reflects another site in the element. No occupied TF has a strong site at the variant.
